verdict.headline: Individual Indonesian tourists need a visa — but groups may not.
verdict.sub: Ordinary passports that require a tourist visa are not eligible for K-ETA for that visit. If your passport requires a visa for a normal mainland visit, K-ETA is not an alternative or an extra application after your visa. K-ETA age exemptions do not waive the visa requirement. Special group and Jeju programs have separate conditions.
verdict.stay: Visa: follow the issued grant; designated group program: 15 days

highlights.title: Group program
highlights.body: Trial: 2026-05-28 to 2026-12-31. Only groups of 3 or more recruited by designated Indonesian agencies qualify, with a maximum 15-day stay. Three independent friends do not qualify. The Korean partner must register the list through HiKorea 24 hours before air arrival or 36 hours before sea arrival and obtain pre-screening; travelers normally enter and leave together on the same flight or ship.

highlights.title: Jeju Island — separate visa-free entry
highlights.body: Indonesian ordinary-passport tourists may use Jeju's separate visa-free program for up to 30 days, arriving directly from overseas and staying on Jeju. Entry via mainland Korea is not covered. Mainland travel requires an appropriate visa or prior immigration permission; entry is assessed at the border.

highlights.title: Multiple entry
highlights.body: Eligible applicants can apply for 5- or 10-year multiple-entry visas; the KVAC table lists a 30-day stay per visit. Long validity does not mean continuous residence or automatic eligibility. Ask KVAC to check your category.

tldr: Independent travelers need a C-3 tourist visa for mainland Korea.

Ordinary-passport tourist visa applications go through KVAC Jakarta. Direct Embassy applications are reserved for diplomatic/official categories and specified exceptional cases; do not go directly to the Embassy for a normal tourist application.

The KVAC tourist checklist includes a copy of the Indonesian family card (Kartu Keluarga). Employees provide an original employment certificate; students an original enrollment certificate; business owners a copy of the business license; homemakers and retirees a copy of KTP. Use the checklist for your category; additional documents may be requested.

funds.title: "How much money should I show?"
funds.body: There is no single published minimum. Show a stable 3-month balance and clear ties to Indonesia (job, family). If someone else funds your trip, document the sponsorship fully.
tips: A steady 3-month balance beats a sudden deposit before applying.
Sponsored? Add the sponsor's bank statement, letter, and relationship proof.

items.q: Do children need their own Korea visa?
items.a: Yes — every traveler, including children, needs their own visa. A minor's application is submitted with a parent's supporting documents and proof of the family relationship.

items.q: How do I pay the visa fees?

items.q: When can I submit and collect my passport?
